heat_spreading_mass.derivation: For lightweight heat spreaders (e.g. aerospace electronics), maximizing thermal conductivity per unit mass gives M = k/ρ.
heat_spreading_mass.name: Heat spreading per unit mass
heat_spreading_mass.scope: Lightweight heat spreaders, mass-limited thermal management.
heat_spreading_mass.source: Ashby, M. F. (2011). Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th ed. §11.7.

max_elastic_energy_vol.derivation: The elastic energy stored per unit volume before yield is σ_y²/(2E).  Maximizing this gives M = σ_y²/E.
max_elastic_energy_vol.name: Max elastic stored energy / volume
max_elastic_energy_vol.source: Ashby, M. F. (2011). Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th ed. Ch. 5–6.

stiff_light_beam.derivation: For a beam of fixed length and prescribed bending stiffness, minimizing mass yields M = E^(1/2)/ρ.  The cross-section is a free variable (can be resized).
stiff_light_beam.name: Stiff, light beam
stiff_light_beam.scope: Fixed length, bending stiffness constraint, free cross-section.
stiff_light_beam.source: Ashby, M. F. (2011). Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th ed. Ch. 5–6.

stiff_light_plate.derivation: For a plate of fixed area loaded in bending, minimizing mass at constant stiffness yields M = E^(1/3)/ρ.  Thickness is the free variable.
stiff_light_plate.name: Stiff, light plate
stiff_light_plate.scope: Fixed area, bending stiffness constraint (plate geometry).
stiff_light_plate.source: Ashby, M. F. (2011). Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th ed. Ch. 5–6.

stiff_light_tie.derivation: For an axially loaded tie of fixed length, minimizing mass at constant axial stiffness yields M = E/ρ.  Derived from F/δ = EA/L with m = ρAL. F: axial force; δ: extension; A: area; L: length; m: mass.
stiff_light_tie.name: Stiff, light tie
stiff_light_tie.source: Ashby, M. F. (2011). Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th ed. Ch. 5–6.

strong_light_beam.derivation: For a beam of fixed length that must not yield in bending, minimizing mass with free cross-section yields M = σ_y^(2/3)/ρ.
strong_light_beam.name: Strong, light beam
strong_light_beam.scope: Fixed length, bending strength, free cross-section.
strong_light_beam.source: Ashby, M. F. (2011). Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th ed. Ch. 5–6.

strong_light_plate.derivation: For a plate of fixed area that must not yield in bending, minimizing mass with free thickness yields M = σ_y^(1/2)/ρ.
strong_light_plate.name: Strong, light plate
strong_light_plate.source: Ashby, M. F. (2011). Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th ed. Ch. 5–6.

strong_light_tie.derivation: For a tie of fixed length that must not yield under axial load, minimizing mass yields M = σ_y/ρ.
strong_light_tie.name: Strong, light tie
strong_light_tie.scope: Fixed length, yield strength in tension.
strong_light_tie.source: Ashby, M. F. (2011). Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th ed. Ch. 5–6.

thermal_insulation.derivation: Minimizing steady-state heat flow through a wall of fixed thickness requires minimizing thermal conductivity.
thermal_insulation.name: Thermal insulation
thermal_insulation.source: Ashby, M. F. (2011). Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th ed. §11.7.

thermal_storage_vol.derivation: The energy stored per unit volume for a given ΔT is ρ·Cₚ·ΔT.  Maximizing ρ·Cₚ maximizes volumetric thermal storage. ΔT: temperature change.
thermal_storage_vol.name: Volumetric thermal storage
thermal_storage_vol.scope: Thermal mass, passive thermal storage.  NOT heat sink performance (which depends on k and convection geometry).
thermal_storage_vol.source: Ashby, M. F. (2011). Materials Selection in Mechanical Design, 4th ed. §11.7.
